proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress repeal Titles I, II and VIII of the Dodd-Frank Act. These create the Financial Stability Oversight Council and its power to single out firms for stricter regulation, the orderly liquidation authority for large failing firms, and the council's power to designate financial market utilities. The chapter argues these provisions entrench too-big-to-fail expectations.
remaining: An act of Congress repealing Titles I, II and VIII, for which no bill or committee action was found.
Finalization of the FSOC guidance, which would narrow but not remove the Title I designation authority.
Any action on the orderly liquidation authority (Title II) or the financial market utility designation power (Title VIII), for which none was found.

status_summary: No repeal of Titles I, II or VIII was found, and no 2025 or 2026 bill to repeal them was identified. The administration has kept the Financial Stability Oversight Council and is changing how it uses its Title I designation power: on 2025-09-10 Treasury Secretary Bessent said the council would revisit its 2023 nonbank guidance, and on 2026-03-30 the council proposed replacing that guidance with a version that raises the threshold for designating a nonbank firm, restores cost-benefit analysis and favors activity-based responses. Comments closed 2026-05-14, and no final version was found. The proposal does not touch Title II or Title VIII, and no action on either was found.

timeline.event: Treasury Secretary Bessent tells the council that it will build financial stability policy around economic growth and economic security, revisit its 2023 nonbank guidance and analytic framework, and use recommendations to member agencies as a more targeted tool than firm designation.

FSOC publishes proposed interpretive guidance on nonbank financial company determinations (91 FR 15551) that would replace the 2023 guidance and rescind the 2023 analytic framework, with a higher designation threshold and restored cost-benefit analysis.
Comment period on the proposed guidance closes; the docket shows 26 comments received at the time of the page capture.

title: Repeal Dodd-Frank Titles I, II and VIII (FSOC designation, orderly liquidation)
uncertainties: Stage is a judgment: the only related action is the proposed FSOC guidance, which narrows use of Title I designation authority but is not a repeal proposal, so it is recorded as a parallel proposal rather than as progress on repeal. The Treasury rulemaking page, as fetched on the date of this pass, listed no FSOC items after November 2023, and a Federal Register query for FSOC documents since 2025-01-20 returned only the 2026-03-30 proposal, so no final guidance was found; the page may lag. Federal Register queries for orderly liquidation (FDIC) and financial market utility designation found nothing on Title II or Title VIII. One web search for a 2025 or 2026 repeal bill returned only older material; congress.gov is blocked to automated fetches, so bills and hearings were not checked directly. The proposal text was read only in part, so statements about it are limited to the parts read. Update 2026-10-15: a Federal Register query for FSOC documents since 2026-04-01 returned none, and Treasury's FSOC rulemaking page still listed nothing after November 2023 (its notices sections were not readable); searches found no 2026 House Financial Services markup on Titles I, II or VIII.
